To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed a multi-functional microelectrode system with a large number of electrodes that enables the simultaneous recording and stimulation of multiple cell parameters.

we have developed a multi-functional CMOS-based micro-electrode array system featuring 59 760 active electrodes, 2048 AP channels, 64 LFP channels, 32 neurotransmitter detection channels, 32 current channels, 32 impedance channels, and 16 dual-mode stimulation channels, and a total of 2048 electrophysiology channels.

we designed a CMOS-based in vitro multi-functional microelectrode system featuring the largest number of electrodes, the largest electrode array area, the highest spatial resolution, the largest number of measurement functions, the highest number of stimulation functions, the highest measurement bandwidth, and the highest number of recording channels.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of high-density microelectrode arrays for in vitro applications.
the development of high-resolution, high-density, multi-channel, and multi-functional microelectrode arrays for in vitro applications.

the development of a CMOS-based multi-functional microelectrode-array system for in vitro electrophysiology and neurochemistry, which is characterized by the highest electrode density, largest electrode area, and largest number of measurement and stimulation functions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the system is a versatile tool for in vitro studies of cellular phenomena and processes.
the device is a unique platform that enables the study of the interdependence of multiple parameters in parallel.

the presented system is the first of its kind to combine six different measurement and stimulation functions and is, at the same time, the largest microelectrode system in terms of the number of electrodes, the number of channels, the active electrode area, and the electrode pitch.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the system enables a wide variety of experiments, such as multi-electrode array recordings and stimulation, impedance measurement, and neurotransmitter detection.

we have designed, fabricated, and tested a microelectrode-based system that integrates a large number of measurement and stimulation functions and that is suitable for studying the complex interactions between multiple cell parameters.
we have developed a microelectrode system with a large electrode density that is capable of measuring multiple cell parameters and performing multiple stimulation functions in parallel.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a single device can be used to simultaneously study multiple aspects of cellular behavior, which will facilitate understanding and modeling of cellular phenomena.
it demonstrates a new level of integration and versatility of in vitro systems, which will enable the study of cellular phenomena and processes with unprecedented detail and complexity.
it is feasible to design and fabricate large-area microelectrode arrays featuring multiple measurement and stimulation functions.
